name: Akiko Global Services Limited
identity_note: Legal name and security checked in cited issuer/exchange filing.
summary: Akiko is a fast-growing credit-distribution business, not a lender earning a spread on its own loan book and not yet a proven cash-generative fintech platform. Strong reported and reviewed growth is offset by recurring cash absorption, related-agent commissions and funding dependence. The fully financed group base case produces a modest return above the hurdle, but reasonable parent-only, minority-mix and working-capital alternatives remove that advantage. Classification: conditional growth watchlist, not a high-conviction compounder. [S1][Q1][PROSP][CALL]

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Akiko is a fast-growing credit-distribution business, not a lender earning a spread on its own loan book and not yet a proven cash-generative fintech platform. Strong reported and reviewed growth is offset by recurring cash absorption, related-agent commissions and funding dependence. The fully financed group base case produces a modest return above the hurdle, but reasonable parent-only, minority-mix and working-capital alternatives remove that advantage. Classification: conditional growth watchlist, not a high-conviction compounder. [S1][Q1][PROSP][CALL]

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Research cutoff 20 October 2026; NSE SME AKIKO, ISIN INE0PMR01017. Dated 19 October close ₹426; an 800-share lot. Forecast horizon ends 19 October 2031 and uses a 15% nominal INR equity hurdle. Annual statements follow Indian GAAP/AS. Constant-parent history is used for long-run growth/cash scoring; current consolidated statements support the group model with explicit minority allocation. Statements are audited, not independently re-audited here. The material AOC-1 conflict is unresolved, not obscured by a generic clean-governance assurance. Current debt/cash after March is modeled through the FY27 cash bridge, not falsely called observed October balances. [S1][Q1][M1]

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: BQS 4.90; Growth Quality GQS 5.00; IAS 5.325. Factors: GOV 4, MOAT 4, REV 8, DUR 6, CAP 6, CASH 3, BAL 4, EXEC 5, EARN 6; R 6, D 4, P 5, L 7. Canonical weights and exact arithmetic are in the structured audit. Persistent CASH 3 caps otherwise higher GQS at 5. R remains 6 because 16.99% is below the 17% band boundary before rounding. Evidence confidence and uncertainty about future growth are different concepts. No missing factor is silently reweighted. Keeping other factors fixed, supported model alternatives shift R from 6 to 5 and IAS from 5.325 to 4.975. This is a scenario range, not a statistical confidence interval.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: The Money Fair sources credit cards and loans for financial institutions through agents, field sales, branches and digital channels. Revenue is recognized for contracted services, rather than being the principal loan disbursement. Management’s July illustration of roughly ₹450 cr monthly loan disbursement and 3.10% payout must therefore not be mistaken for ₹450 cr revenue. FY26 group purchase of services ₹104.9314 cr includes ₹91.1199 cr DSA/FOS commissions and ₹13.8115 cr data/support costs; employee costs were ₹30.5911 cr. Distribution is labor- and customer-acquisition-intensive despite modest fixed assets. Subsidiaries are White Lotus 51%, M11 75%, Dubai commercial broker 70%. AkikoPay is integrated with core distribution: adding its aspirational sales again would double count. [S1][CALL][MAY]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Bank relationships and lead-processing infrastructure support scale, but lender payout terms, credit appetite and competing channels limit pricing power. The IPO prospectus reported 93.26% of FY23 sales from the top 10 customers; this is historical, not proof of current concentration or diversification. PB Fintech’s primary FAQ describes Paisabazaar as a marketplace comparing and facilitating personal-credit applications. That is a relevant competitive model, but PB’s insurance scale, brand, cash and economics are not interchangeable with Akiko, so no PB multiple is copied. Claims that AkikoPay can compete with much larger payment platforms are aspirations; paid retention, repeat conversion, customer-acquisition payback and incremental profit have not been independently demonstrated. [PROSP][PEER][CALL]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Parent revenue FY21–FY26:₹6.1078/13.5192/39.5811/32.1993/63.4513/122.3924 cr. Five-year CAGR 82.13%; three-year CAGR 45.69%. FY24 contracted 18.65%, followed by additions ₹31.2520 cr and ₹58.9411 cr in FY25/FY26. This is strong but non-linear growth, not six years of uninterrupted compounding. Group FY26 sales ₹172.7316 cr versus ₹76.3022 cr also reflect a full year of subsidiaries acquired during FY25. Reviewed Q1 FY27 group sales ₹68.1218 cr versus ₹29.5358 cr; parent ₹59.1087 cr versus ₹20.8586 cr. October 19 estimated H1 sales ₹151.57 cr versus ₹63.08 cr imply 140.28% growth, not the table’s printed 240%, which is approximately the ratio expressed as a percentage. September ₹29.60 cr versus ₹17.34 cr implies 70.70%. These turnover estimates are not audited H1 profit or cash. [PROSP][H25][S1][Q1][SEPT]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: Management described 25 leased branches across 19 cities and raised FY27 guidance to ₹325–350 cr, while aspiring to 70–100% growth for three years. The base model uses ₹300 cr then 30/25/20/15/10% growth, materially below that aspiration. Base EBITDA 15% approximates FY26 group 14.51% and reviewed Q1 roughly 14.82%; it is not an assumed software margin. IPO ERP/Tele CRM spending still had ₹0.70 cr unutilized at June; ₹2 cr software under development at March was already spent and is not charged twice. Purchased data/support costs were historically amortized one-third in the current year and two-thirds over subsequent use. This can support repeat distribution, but ₹14.1336 cr group prepaids and ₹14.3602 cr vendor advances require cash financing and evidence of conversion, not merely an app-download narrative. [PROSP][S1][Q1][CALL]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: Related Card Experties India commission rose from ₹1.8387 cr to ₹22.8599 cr, about 25.1% of group DSA/FOS commissions. Disclosed related remuneration, rents/fees and loans require minority-economic scrutiny, without assuming disclosed related transactions are improper. Parent loans outstanding ₹10.7736 cr include ₹7.5526 cr to subsidiaries; repayment/interest schedules are on demand or unspecified. Group director borrowings ₹4.0554 cr support funding but may be callable. CARO reports TDS/GST including interest/fees ₹0.3296/0.0184 cr overdue beyond six months; financial expenses also include ₹0.4403 cr interest on delayed statutory payments. September 2 Ankur Gaba became MD; Priyanka moved to executive director effective September 10, and Richa resigned as executive director. That filing alone does not establish resignation as CFO. Independent director Tarun resigned October 8 citing personal reasons and no other material reasons. February 10 IPO-use-format clarification points to existing disclosures; it is not an admitted diversion of proceeds. AGM expansion to 675000 ESOPs, not only the incremental 375000 approval, and 200000 warrants are incorporated in potential dilution. [S1][BOARD][U2][U1][AGM][S2]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
Parent FY24/FY25/FY26 PAT ₹3.7545/5.9587/11.2869 cr compares with CFO −₹6.2845/−₹9.6879/−₹1.7638 cr and capex ₹0.0680/4.4555/2.1426 cr. Three-year CFO/PAT is −84.46%, before financing costs classified separately. FY25 CFO originally −₹11.1607 cr was recast by moving ₹1.4728 cr long-term loans/deposits to investing: the reclassification is explained, not called new cash. Group FY25 CFO begins with zero opening group balances despite the operating parent; it cannot be spliced into a comparable multiyear ratio. FY26 group CFO −₹5.6731 cr less capex ₹2.4372 cr gives −₹8.1103 cr before additional long-term loans. Parent operating EBIT ₹15.9755 cr excludes ₹0.2680 cr other income; 25% NOPAT return on average equity-plus-debt is 21.77%, but cash realization remains weaker.

The final prospectus explicitly explains three-year data/support-cost deferral. Parent prepaids actually FALL from ₹11.8812 cr to ₹10.9443 cr in FY26, so the stock of prepaids does not prove current parent profit inflation. Group prepaids rise ₹1.2069 cr. The receivable ageing table places all ₹63.236 cr under a “doubtful” row while the same note says considered good and provides no allowance. This recurring label conflict is visually verified; it does not prove ₹63 cr is uncollectible. Only ₹0.4259 cr is shown older than six months, but post-period collections were not independently confirmed.

More materially, on the INR-lakh interpretation consistent with the prior capital presentation, AOC-1 subsidiary PAT sums ₹1.7049 cr, while the group auditor’s Other Matters says ₹6.1281 cr, a ₹4.4232 cr gap or 25.4% of group PAT. The latter exactly bridges parent ₹11.2869 cr to group ₹17.415 cr. Public subsidiary files retrieved cover FY25 and do not resolve FY26. The audit statements remain the model anchor, with parent-only and explicit earnings-gap stress, not an assertion the annexure discrepancy is cured. [PROSP][H25][S1][SUB][SUB25]

Scope checks: AOC-1 explicitly marks alternative reporting periods “NA”, gives acquisition dates before 1 April 2025 for all three subsidiaries, and shows no different FY26 control period. The consolidated auditor expressly refers to the year ended 31 March 2026. Dubai’s AOC-1 column lists AED and an exchange rate of ₹25.5, but the annexure caption says only amounts in rupees, without a clear scale. Its capital 92.96 matches the prior INR-lakh presentation; the retrieved FY25 Dubai audit is an INR special-purpose consolidation report. Ordinary translation using ₹25.5 rather than prior ₹23.24 does not bridge the profit gap. Literal AED or rupee interpretations produce very different totals, not the auditor subtotal. Thus ₹4.4232 cr is a conditional like-unit discrepancy, not a certified overstatement. Current subsidiary reports or an issuer bridge could still explain it. [S1][H25][SUB][SUBFX]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
Five-year fully financed base/bear/bull terminal prices are ₹933.56/₹150.95/₹2536.39; IRRs 16.99%/−18.74%/+42.88%. Base 15% hurdle entry ₹464.15 provides limited room above ₹426. Base starts with group ₹300 cr FY27 sales, 15% EBITDA, 40% economic WC/sales and 2% capex. FY27–FY31 annual statements plus a FY32 April–October stub reach the exact five-year terminal date. Base exit 16 times operating NOPAT is an analyst assumption, not an observed comparable multiple. Model funding costs 14%, tax 25%, a ₹2 cr operating reserve, net current tax settlement once and a blended four-year asset life. Known overdue TDS/GST is removed from opening WC and settled once; no second blanket tax reserve is invented.

Base requires ₹32.96 cr new debt. Debt capacity is analytically capped at 2 times annual EBITDA, not claimed as a sanctioned covenant; any residual deficit requires hypothetical equity at 30% below the dated quote with 3% fees. 675000 potential ESOP shares plus 200000 warrants lift initial diluted shares to 1.16446 cr, without unreceived exercise cash. Group value allocates 12% to minority economics, based on FY26 profit mix, not a legal parent ownership percentage. Parent-only base gives 14.45%; minority allocation 25% gives 13.31%; 50% WC gives 14.99%; a recurring ₹4.4232 cr after-tax earnings reduction (grossed up at 25% tax) gives 14.97%. These are comparisons, not asserted corrections to audited earnings. Forecast details and cash/debt/equity reconciliations are attached. [S1][Q1][SEPT][AGM][S2][M1]

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: Bear revenue starts ₹250 cr, consistent with a much weaker H2 after estimated H1 ₹151.57 cr, then stagnates before modest growth. 10% EBITDA and 50% WC force ₹35.10 cr debt draws plus ₹21.93 cr gross equity, leaving a 64.6% price loss. Severe case ₹47.51 per share presupposes ₹84.44 cr gross equity; inability to raise capital can instead leave no recoverable equity. Banking-partner payout cuts, higher acquisition costs, stale data, vendor advances that fail to convert, or withdrawal of director funding can reinforce one another. ₹8/20 cr cash-loss stresses are hypothetical portfolio shocks, not expected fraud losses. The AOC-1 gap, demand loans and data-cost deferral increase the need for verified cash collection. Ordinary tax claims are not transformed into arbitrary multimillion-rupee penalties. [S1][PROSP][CALL] Bear/severe and prepaid-loss sensitivities impair opening recoverable operating assets, reducing opening working capital before calculating replacement funding. The noncash expense is charged to PAT and added back in CFO; the required closing working-capital stock is funded once. No separate immediate cash payment or tax shield is assumed. This explicit stock-and-flow bridge leaves the previously reported terminal prices, IRRs and scores unchanged.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: Five/ten times ₹426 require ₹2130/₹4260 per share. At 20 times terminal attributable PAT and 1.16446 cr initial potential shares, required owner profits are ₹124.01/₹248.03 cr, versus FY26 ₹15.3275 cr. At 10% group PAT margin and 88% attribution, implied annual revenue is roughly ₹1409/₹2819 cr; future financing dilution would increase the requirement. The bull case crosses 5 times only with sustained aggressive expansion, 18% EBITDA, 33% WC and 20 times NOPAT valuation. It is a demanding joint outcome, not a price target derived solely from management’s 70–100% growth ambition. [S1][CALL][AGM][M1]

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Track: (1) audited H1 sales/profit versus ₹151.57 cr estimated sales and the corrected growth calculation; (2) operating receipts, vendor advances, prepaid amortization and actual bank/funding balances; (3) reconciliation of subsidiary AOC-1 against audited individual accounts and minority allocation; (4) Card Experties commission terms, balances and measurable service delivery; (5) app active users, paid conversion, repeat use and acquisition payback without duplicate core revenue; (6) any actual ESOP grants, warrant conversion, exercise proceeds and trust loans; (7) statutory arrears, interest cost and director-demand funding; (8) board/CFO succession and live lot-level execution. A second strong profit period without cash conversion, or financing unavailable at modeled cost, invalidates the optimistic interpretation. [S1][Q1][SEPT][CALL][BOARD][S2]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Conditional growth watchlist. BQS 4.90 and capped GQS 5.00 do not support calling this a proven quality compounder; IAS 5.325 depends on the audited group anchor and funded assumptions. A modest model spread over the 15% hurdle is not robust to minority mix or cash-cycle deterioration. Valuation work is complete as conditional scenarios, while the subsidiary discrepancy remains an evidence limitation requiring resolution before high-conviction underwriting.

All 60 sessions were observed. Conservative 20-session turnover ₹54.5194 lakh is slower than the 60-session ₹61.1628 lakh; a ₹5 lakh exit at 5% participation takes 1.83 days arithmetically. One 800-share lot costs ₹340800, so a ₹5 lakh reference position cannot be precisely implemented as fractional lots. L 7 incorporates a two-point downgrade for lot granularity, narrow PAN breadth, large price-variation alerts and absent live spread/depth. October 19 REG1 applies October 21; inactive ESM/ASM/GSM flags are not universal clearance. Generic irregular-trading caution does not fabricate missing market days. [M1][REG1][REGFMT][S1]

G 2 is conditional rather than critical-fail for this published model because the aggregate audited income/financial-position statements, matching parent/group profit bridge and subsequent independently reviewed Q1 support its material inputs at Medium confidence. The unreliable component annexure is not used to allocate operating growth, cash or individual subsidiary multiples. Parent-only and after-tax discrepancy stresses move IAS to 4.975 but do not change the watchlist classification. This does not certify the annexure or clear the entire group. An auditor correction, unsupported aggregate balance, or incompatible current subsidiary reports would invalidate that hierarchy and make IAS NS pending reconciliation.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Primary evidence comprises FY25/FY26 annual reports, final IPO prospectus, reviewed Q1, management-call transcripts, October turnover/ESOP filings, September board/AGM documents and official NSE market data. Peer evidence is an operating-model comparison only. Source PDFs, exact links, calculation inputs and annual financed scenarios are retained. Current live collections, collateral availability, approved new credit and app unit economics are not independently observed. AOC-1/current subsidiary profit remains unreconciled after checking issuer subsidiary links; current group forecasts use the higher-level audited statement hierarchy and explicit sensitivities, not fabricated certainty. No guaranteed future funding, hidden expected tax bill or automatic equity issue is assumed. [S1][H25][PROSP][Q1][SUB][M1]

score_note: Canonical factors; persistent CASH3 caps Growth Quality at5. Conditional group valuation includes financed downside and a parent-only cross-check. Material subsidiary-annexure reconciliation remains unresolved, not hidden. G2 rationale distinguishes aggregate audited inputs from unreliable component annexure. Holding other factors fixed, parent-only and after-tax gap stresses imply IAS4.975versusbase5.325, same watchlist conclusion. A future material aggregate correction would requireIASNS.

GOV.reason: Related Card Experties commission ₹22.8599 cr versus ₹1.8387 cr, demand loans, statutory delays and material AOC-1/CFS reconciliation gap warrant a control discount. Unqualified audited statements and subsequent reviewed quarterly results remain stronger anchors than the inconsistent annexure. No allegation of fraud or automatic resignation penalty.

MOAT.reason: Bank relationships, distribution and technology support execution, but other DSAs, direct bank channels and Paisabazaar compete for the same customers. No demonstrated proprietary data exclusivity, durable commission pricing or measured app retention. Historical top 10 customer concentration 93.26%.

REV.reason: Parent FY21–26 revenue ₹6.1078/13.5192/39.5811/32.1993/63.4513/122.3924 cr: five-year CAGR 82.13%, baseline 9 minus 1 for FY24 contraction and unseparated volume/payout mix. Parent history avoids acquisition-spliced group CAGR; current group growth 126.38% is not all organic.

DUR.reason: Lending distribution, branches and cross-selling create runway; reviewed Q1 and estimated H1 support near-term demand. Funding, banking-partner policies and unproven AkikoPay retention constrain duration. Management 70–100% growth aspiration is not a contracted backlog.

CAP.reason: Parent operating EBIT₹15.9755 cr, normalized 25% NOPAT₹11.9816 cr and average equity-plus-debt ₹55.0401 cr imply 21.77% operating return; incremental return approximately 24.67%. Productive growth is offset by ₹10.7736 cr parent loans and heavy data/vendor working capital, so accounting ROCE does not establish cash capital efficiency.

CASH.reason: Parent FY24/FY25 recast/FY26 CFO −₹6.2845/−₹9.6879/−₹1.7638 cr totals −₹17.7362 cr against ₹21.0001 cr PAT. Original FY25 CFO −₹11.1607 cr improves only because ₹1.4728 cr loans/deposits move to investing. Three weak years establish persistence. FY26 group CFO −₹5.6731 cr and growing vendor advances reinforce the diagnosis, without treating growth investment as misconduct.

BAL.reason: Group debt ₹14.8961 cr versus ₹3.2781 cr cash, net current tax ₹1.935 cr and recurring working-capital demands leave limited internal headroom. Some unsecured loan rates 16–19.64% and director demand funding are meaningful. Base requires ₹32.96 cr new debt; no availability is assumed.

EXEC.reason: Reviewed Q1 growth and branch scaling are tangible. App launch/feature delays, no separately verified app unit economics, related commission scale and weak collection conversion prevent a high execution score. July no-equity-raise expectation is tested against financed scenarios rather than accepted as proof.

EARN.reason: Parent PAT₹11.2869 cr versus ₹5.9587 cr and operating profit both rise; parent EPS₹10.48 versus ₹6.10 grows less than PAT after IPO weighting. Groupowner PAT₹15.3275 cr and reviewed Q1 ₹6.8946 cr are strong, but deferred data costs, cash conversion, subsidiary-annexure mismatch and potential share dilution limit quality.

R.reason: Fully funded base five-year IRR 16.99%, about 1.99 points above 15% hurdle, falls in band 6, not band 7 after premature rounding. Parent-only 14.45%, higher minority 13.31% and WC 50% 14.99% demonstrate sensitivity. This is conditional model output, not a promised return.

D.reason: Bear terminal ₹150.95 is a 64.6% price loss and needs ₹21.93 cr hypothetical gross equity plus ₹35.10 cr debt. Severe terminal ₹47.51 assumes ₹84.44 cr gross equity; without willing capital providers the outcome can be zero. Required financing and dilution, not merely multiple volatility, drive permanent-loss risk.

P.reason: At ₹426, reported FY26 owner EPS implies 29.94 x PE; full potential shares increase this to 32.37 x. Model hurdle entry ₹464.15 offers only 9% cushion and depends on funded expansion; the parent-only hurdle is belowquote. Neither a cheap cash compounder nor an automatic rejection of all growth value.

L.reason: All 60 sessions observed. Slower 20-session conservative turnover ₹54.5194 lakh versus 60-session ₹61.1628 lakh gives 1.83 days for ₹5 lakh at 5% participation, startingband 9. Two-point downgrade reflects ₹340800 whole lot, narrow PAN breadth, large price-movement alerts and unobserved live spread/depth; generic SME caution is not a no-trade-day count.

valuation.status: Conditional, explicitly financed forecast; group audit hierarchy with parent-only cross-check and unresolved AOC-1 reconciliation
assumption_basis: FY 26 audited statements are the primary financial anchor. The AOC-1 subsidiary-profit sum conflicts materially with the auditor’s consolidated subtotal. No claim of proven overstatement is made. Parent-only cross-check and recurring-cost sensitivity (after-tax gap grossed up at 25%) show consequence without inventing an expected correction.

FY 27 group revenue 300 crore is below July management guidance 325–350 crore, and near twice estimated H 1 sales 151.57 crore. Parent 240 crore is near four times reviewed Q 1 sales 59.1087 crore. These are scenarios, not achieved results. Subsequent base growth 30/25/20/15/10% is far below management’s 70–100% three-year aspiration.

Base 15% EBITDA margin approximates FY 26 group 14.51% and Q 1 FY 27 14.82%; bear 10% and bull 18% require different acquisition-cost outcomes. Deferred marketing/data cost and prepaid investment are funded through working capital. No separate AkikoPay sales are added to already integrated core sales.

Opening economic WC 66.4956 crore group,48.6148 crore parent includes data prepayments, vendor advances, security deposits, trade debtors and operating creditors/provisions. Excludes tax assets/liabilities settled once, interest accrued separately restored, and non-operating loans that receive no incremental base value. Fixed deposit 0.6 crore excluded from free cash; no automatic maturity release.

Net tax liability 1.935 crore group (2.1947 minus 0.2597) or 1.4011 crore parent is settled once. Other statutory liabilities remain in WC; known overdue TDS/GST 0.3480 crore is removed from opening WC and settled once. Accrued interest 0.0433 crore is separately settled once. Ordinary disputed-tax claims are sensitivities, not unsupported new expected liabilities.

Opening reserve 2 crore is an analyst minimum, not cash available for distributions. Capex 2% sales base/bear includes the 0.7 crore ERP amount outstanding at June; already-spent 2 crore software development is in opening PPE, not spent twice. Blended four-year depreciation and 25% tax on positive PBT.

Funding 14% includes half-year interest on new debt; FY 26 disclosed unsecured rates 16–19.64% and secured 10.15%, alongside low/no-rate directors funding, support a normalized rate above reported historical average. Analytical debt ceiling 2 x annual EBITDA is not an actual covenant or sanctioned limit. Remaining gaps require equity at 30% discount to dated 426 price plus 3% fees, explicitly hypothetical and not authorized financing. Severe no-funding outcome can be zero irrespective of conditional model value.

FY 26 issued 10.7696 m shares plus 675000 ESOP maximum approved September and 200000 warrants produce 11.6446 m potential shares. No unreceived exercise cash is credited. Further modeled financing dilutes this denominator. ESOP ceiling is not actual grant/exercise; denominator is conservative.

A 12% minority economic profit/value allocation approximates FY 26 minority 2.0875/17.415, not a legal stake in the parent. Q 1 mix was much lower.25% sensitivity and parent-only model address mix uncertainty; no minority cash is claimed wholly for parent.

FY 27–FY 31 annual schedules plus FY 32 April–October stub end exactly five years after entry. The full FY 27 forecast also bridges unreported March–October balance-sheet movements; it is not a statement of observed current debt/cash. No pre-entry cash dividends are counted. Terminal operating NOPAT multiples 12/16/20 (severe 10) are analyst assumptions, not copied PB Fintech multiples.

Bear, severe and prepaid-loss cases are noncash impairments of opening recoverable operating assets, not separate cash obligations. Reduce opening recoverable WC, charge PAT, add the impairment back in CFO, then fund the target closing WC. Lost collections/replacement funding enter once through that WC bridge. No immediate cash payment or assumed tax shield is invented.
